title: 谷歌创始人信：怎样介绍公司的工作方式（2004）
topic: 谷歌创始人信：怎样介绍公司的工作方式（2004）

source.title: A letter from Larry and Sergey
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 原文出自 Google 谷歌 公开资料。
paragraphs: Our very first founders’ letter in our 2004 S-1 began:

“Google is not a conventional company. We do not intend to become one. Throughout Google’s evolution as a privately held company, we have managed Google differently. We have also emphasized an atmosphere of creativity and challenge, which has helped us provide unbiased, accurate and free access to information for those who rely on us around the world.”

We believe those central tenets are still true today. The company is not conventional and continues to make ambitious bets on new technology, especially with our Alphabet structure. Creativity and challenge remain as ever-present as before, if not more so, and are increasingly applied to a variety of fields such as machine learning, energy efficiency and transportation. Nonetheless, Google’s core service—providing unbiased, accurate, and free access to information—remains at the heart of the company.

However, since we wrote our first founders’ letter, the company has evolved and matured. Within Google, there are all the popular consumer services that followed Search, such as Maps, Photos, and YouTube; a global ecosystem of devices powered by our Android and Chrome platforms, including our own Made by Google devices; Google Cloud, including GCP and G Suite; and of course a base of fundamental technologies around machine learning, cloud computing, and software engineering. It’s an honor that billions of people have chosen to make these products central to their lives—this is a trust and responsibility that Google will always work to live up to.
translations: 我们2004年S-1文件中的第一封创始人信开头写道：
“谷歌不是一家传统公司。我们并不打算成为一家传统公司。在谷歌作为私人控股公司的发展过程中，我们一直以不同的方式管理谷歌。我们还强调创造力和挑战的氛围，这帮助我们为世界各地依赖我们的人们提供无偏见、准确且免费的信息获取。”
我们相信这些核心原则在今天仍然成立。这家公司并非传统公司，并且继续在新技术上做出大胆的押注，尤其是在我们的Alphabet结构下。创造力和挑战一如既往地存在，甚至比以往更甚，并且越来越多地应用于机器学习、能源效率和交通等各个领域。尽管如此，谷歌的核心服务——提供无偏见、准确且免费的信息获取——仍然是公司的核心。

然而，自从我们写下第一封创始人信以来，公司已经发展和成熟。在谷歌内部，有继搜索之后的所有流行的消费者服务，如地图、照片和YouTube；由我们的Android和Chrome平台驱动的全球设备生态系统，包括我们自己制造的谷歌设备；谷歌云，包括GCP和G Suite；当然还有围绕机器学习、云计算和软件工程的一系列基础技术。数十亿人选择将这些产品作为他们生活的中心，这是一种荣誉——谷歌将永远努力不辜负这份信任和责任。
fullTextParagraphs: Our very first founders’ letter in our 2004 S-1 began:

“Google is not a conventional company. We do not intend to become one. Throughout Google’s evolution as a privately held company, we have managed Google differently. We have also emphasized an atmosphere of creativity and challenge, which has helped us provide unbiased, accurate and free access to information for those who rely on us around the world.”

We believe those central tenets are still true today. The company is not conventional and continues to make ambitious bets on new technology, especially with our Alphabet structure. Creativity and challenge remain as ever-present as before, if not more so, and are increasingly applied to a variety of fields such as machine learning, energy efficiency and transportation. Nonetheless, Google’s core service—providing unbiased, accurate, and free access to information—remains at the heart of the company.

However, since we wrote our first founders’ letter, the company has evolved and matured. Within Google, there are all the popular consumer services that followed Search, such as Maps, Photos, and YouTube; a global ecosystem of devices powered by our Android and Chrome platforms, including our own Made by Google devices; Google Cloud, including GCP and G Suite; and of course a base of fundamental technologies around machine learning, cloud computing, and software engineering. It’s an honor that billions of people have chosen to make these products central to their lives—this is a trust and responsibility that Google will always work to live up to.
And structurally, the company evolved into Alphabet in 2015. As we said in the Alphabet founding letter in 2015:
“Alphabet is about businesses prospering through strong leaders and independence.”

Since we wrote that, hundreds of Phoenix residents are now being driven around in Waymo cars—many without drivers! Wing became the first drone company to make commercial deliveries to consumers in the U.S. And Verily and Calico are doing important work, through a number of great partnerships with other healthcare companies. Some of our “Other Bets” have their own boards with independent members, and outside investors.

Those are just a few examples of technology companies that we have formed within Alphabet, in addition to investment subsidiaries GV and Capital G, which have supported hundreds more. Together with all of Google’s services, this forms a colorful tapestry of bets in technology across a range of industries—all with the goal of helping people and tackling major challenges.
“Google was born in 1998. If it were a person, it would have started elementary school late last summer (around August 19), and today it would have just about finished the first grade.”

Today, in 2019, if the company was a person, it would be a young adult of 21 and it would be time to leave the roost. While it has been a tremendous privilege to be deeply involved in the day-to-day management of the company for so long, we believe it’s time to assume the role of proud parents—offering advice and love, but not daily nagging!

With Alphabet now well-established, and Google and the Other Bets operating effectively as independent companies, it’s the natural time to simplify our management structure. We’ve never been ones to hold on to management roles when we think there’s a better way to run the company. And Alphabet and Google no longer need two CEOs and a President. Going forward, Sundar will be the CEO of both Google and Alphabet. He will be the executive responsible and accountable for leading Google, and managing Alphabet’s investment in our portfolio of Other Bets. We are deeply committed to Google and Alphabet for the long term, and will remain actively involved as Board members, shareholders and co-founders. In addition, we plan to continue talking with Sundar regularly, especially on topics we’re passionate about!

Sundar brings humility and a deep passion for technology to our users, partners and our employees every day. He’s worked closely with us for 15 years, through the formation of Alphabet, as CEO of Google, and a member of the Alphabet Board of Directors. He shares our confidence in the value of the Alphabet structure, and the ability it provides us to tackle big challenges through technology. There is no one that we have relied on more since Alphabet was founded, and no better person to lead Google and Alphabet into the future.

We are deeply humbled to have seen a small research project develop into a source of knowledge and empowerment for billions—a bet we made as two Stanford students that led to a multitude of other technology bets. We could not have imagined, back in 1998 when we moved our servers from a dorm room to a garage, the journey that would follow.

When I was visiting Googlers in Tokyo a few weeks ago I talked about how Google has changed over the years. In fact, in my 15+ years with Google, the only constant I’ve seen is change. This process of continuous evolution -- which the founders often refer to as "uncomfortably exciting" -- is part of who we are. That statement will feel particularly true today as you read the news Larry and Sergey have just posted to our blog.
The key message Larry and Sergey shared is this:

While it has been a tremendous privilege to be deeply involved in the day-to-day management of the company for so long, we believe it’s time to assume the role of proud parents—offering advice and love, but not daily nagging!

I first met Larry and Sergey back in 2004 and have been benefiting from their guidance and insights ever since. The good news is I’ll continue to work with them -- although in different roles for them and me. They’ll still be around to advise as board members and co-founders.

I want to be clear that this transition won't affect the Alphabet structure or the work we do day to day. I will continue to be very focused on Google and the deep work we’re doing to push the boundaries of computing and build a more helpful Google for everyone. At the same time, I’m excited about Alphabet and its long term focus on tackling big challenges through technology.

The founders have given all of us an incredible chance to have an impact on the world. Thanks to them, we have a timeless mission, enduring values, and a culture of collaboration and exploration that makes it exciting to come to work every day. It’s a strong foundation on which we will continue to build. Can’t wait to see where we go next and look forward to continuing the journey with all of you.
Read an edited transcript of Sundar Pichai’s remarks from the Q2 2026 Alphabet earnings call.

notes.explain: 指公司创始人撰写的公开信，通常在公司上市或重要里程碑时发布，阐述公司愿景和价值观
notes.example: The founders' letter in the annual report outlines the company's long-term vision and commitment to innovation.

notes.phrase: unbiased, accurate and free access to information
notes.meaning: 对信息的无偏见、准确和免费获取
notes.explain: 谷歌的核心使命，强调提供客观、可靠且无需付费的信息服务
notes.example: Our mission is to ensure unbiased, accurate and free access to information for everyone, regardless of their location or background.

notes.explain: 指公司最基本、最重要的价值观或信念，是公司决策和行为的指导原则
notes.example: The company's central tenets of innovation and customer focus remain unchanged despite market challenges.

notes.explain: 指支撑公司核心业务和产品开发的关键技术，通常是公司长期投入和积累的领域
notes.example: Our investment in fundamental technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum computing positions us for future growth.

scenario.title: Explain Google’s original company philosophy
english: A new colleague asks what Google said about its company culture and mission in the founders’ 2004 letter.
You explain that the letter described Google as unconventional and connected a creative, challenging atmosphere with its goal of providing unbiased, accurate, and free access to information.
Your colleague gets a concise summary of both the company’s approach and its stated mission at that time.
chinese: 一位新同事问，Google 创始人在 2004 年的信中如何描述公司的工作方式和使命。
你说明，信中称 Google 不走寻常路，并把鼓励创造与挑战的氛围，同提供公正、准确、免费信息的使命联系起来。
同事由此了解了当时信中对公司工作方式和使命的概括。

firstAttempt.prompt: 你要给新同事介绍团队的工作方式和使命。请用两句英文说明团队如何鼓励创造与挑战，以及这如何服务用户。
firstAttempt.sample: We emphasize an atmosphere of creativity and challenge. Providing unbiased, accurate, and free access to information remains at the heart of our work.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先介绍工作氛围，再说明这与团队为用户提供的信息服务如何相连。

words.collocation: run a conventional company, not a conventional company
words.example: We don't want to be just another conventional company; we aim to disrupt the industry with our innovative approach.
words.translation: 我们不想成为又一家传统公司；我们希望通过创新方法颠覆这个行业。
words.note: 用于描述遵循传统商业模式和结构的公司，通常暗示缺乏创新

words.example: The evolution of our business model has allowed us to adapt to changing market demands.
words.translation: 我们商业模式的演变使我们能够适应不断变化的市场需求。
words.note: 描述渐进式发展和变化的过程，强调自然而非革命性的转变

words.collocation: make ambitious bets on, ambitious bets in
words.example: The company is making ambitious bets on emerging technologies to secure its future position in the market.
words.translation: 公司正在对新兴技术进行雄心勃勃的押注，以确保其在市场上的未来地位。
words.note: 用于描述对高风险、高回报项目的战略性投资

words.example: Our goal is to build a comprehensive ecosystem of products and services that work seamlessly together.
words.translation: 我们的目标是构建一个产品和服务无缝协作的综合生态系统。
words.note: 在商业语境中，指相互依存的产品、服务和合作伙伴网络

words.collocation: live up to expectations, live up to one's reputation
words.example: As a market leader, we must constantly innovate to live up to our customers' expectations.
words.translation: 作为市场领导者，我们必须不断创新，以满足客户的期望。
words.note: 表示达到某种标准、期望或声誉，常用于表达责任感

words.example: Understanding the fundamental concepts of the industry is crucial for new employees.
words.translation: 理解行业的基本概念对新员工至关重要。
words.note: 强调某事物是基础性的、必不可少的，是更复杂事物的基础

structure.original: Throughout Google’s evolution as a privately held company, we have managed Google differently.
analysis: 介词短语'Throughout Google's evolution as a privately held company'作时间状语，修饰整个句子，表示'在谷歌作为私营公司的发展历程中'
主句为'we have managed Google differently'，现在完成时态表示从过去持续到现在的动作
'differently'为副词，修饰动词'managed'，表示'以不同的方式'
structure.transfer: Across projects, we value open discussion and practical problem-solving to make useful information easier to find.

rewrite.bad: We do good work and want customers to like our products.
rewrite.good: We value open discussion and practical problem-solving. Our goal is to make it easier for customers to find the information they need.
rewrite.translation: 我们重视开放讨论和务实的问题解决方式。我们的目标是让客户更容易找到所需信息。
rewrite.pattern: We value [a way of working]. Our goal is to make it easier for [people] to [do something useful].

cloze.prompt: We emphasize an atmosphere of creativity and ___.
cloze.why: creativity and challenge 概括原文提到的工作氛围。

cloze.prompt: Our goal is to provide unbiased, accurate, and free access ___ information.
cloze.why: access to information 是固定搭配。

cloze.prompt: Providing accurate information remains at the ___ of our work.
cloze.why: at the heart of 表示处于核心位置。

dictation.text: Sarah, a project manager, was tasked with implementing new reporting procedures after her department's leadership changed.
She needed to coordinate with her team while adjusting to the new management's directives.

translationPractice.prompt: 我们强调营造鼓励创造与挑战的氛围。
translationPractice.answer: We emphasize an atmosphere of creativity and challenge.

translationPractice.prompt: 我们的目标是提供公正、准确且免费的信息获取服务。
translationPractice.answer: Our goal is to provide unbiased, accurate, and free access to information.

translationPractice.prompt: 提供准确信息仍是我们工作的核心。
translationPractice.answer: Providing accurate information remains at the heart of our work.

choice.prompt: 请用两句英文向新同事介绍 Google 创始人信中的工作氛围和核心使命。
options: We emphasize an atmosphere of creativity and challenge. Providing unbiased, accurate, and free access to information remains at the heart of our work.
We follow the same process as every other company. Our goal is to sell more products this quarter.
Could we share an example of a difficult decision? It may help the team understand what happened.
choice.why: 第一句说明工作氛围，第二句说明原文所述的信息服务使命。

output.prompt: 新同事问团队扩展到多个产品后，是否还坚持原来的使命。请用英文介绍团队鼓励的工作氛围，以及为用户提供的信息服务仍处于工作的核心。
output.sample: We encourage creativity and challenge as we explore new products. Providing unbiased, accurate, and accessible information remains at the heart of our work.
check: 是否说明团队的工作方式或价值取向？
是否说明工作希望带来的结果？
是否把模拟表达与 Google 2004 年原信区分开？
